name: Phase 4 tools: parallel tool calls + batch (F07), tool search (F08), explicit prompt-cache markers (F10 C3)
description: F07: run_agent handles a turn's tool calls in three steps. Step 1, in call order: each call gets its ToolStart row and its permission check (a future pre_tool hook goes beside permitted()); a batch call is opened into its {name, args} calls here, each with its own row and permission, and a nested batch is refused. Step 2: parallel_groups cuts the calls into maximal runs of parallel-safe tools (read_file, grep, glob, list_dir, job_output, run_command, run_background, web_fetch, MCP; D6) joined with futures_util join_all, sync ones on tokio's blocking pool (works on the current_thread runtime); every other call (writes, ask_user, delegate, todo, job_stop, tool_search) runs alone in its place, so a read after a write sees it. Step 3: results join the session in call order; a batch's results become one tool result with a header per call. ToolStart/ToolEnd carry a process-unique id and the TUI keeps tool_rows (id, line, waited-on-permission) so rows settle in any order, failure output is inserted under its own row. PENDING_IMAGE became a list. MCP requests hold the server's reader lock from send to reply, so two parallel calls to one server take turns. F08: "defer": true on an MCP server keeps its tools out of tool_schemas; while any server is deferred a built-in tool_search {query, limit?} (default 5, max 8) is declared, naming each deferred server and its tool count; it ranks the deferred tools not yet loaded with BM25 (k1 1.2, b 0.75) over server, name (camelCase and _ split), description and parameter names/descriptions, stop words dropped, naive plural/-ing stem, and records the loaded names on its tool entry (Entry.loaded). tool_schemas is rebuilt per request from Session::loaded() on the active path, loads appended last, so they survive resume and /tree and stay on their branch; compaction carries loads onto the summary entry. F10 C3: "cache": "anthropic" | "openai" on a model profile (CacheMode enum; an unknown value is a parse error), default off; anthropic puts cache_control {type: ephemeral} on the system prompt, the last tool and the newest message with text (a tool result included); openai sends prompt_cache_key = FNV-1a of the session file's absolute path.
evidence: cargo test (all pass, 86): ai_core::parallel_calls_overlap_and_report_in_call_order (a 3 s and a 2 s command overlap under 4.5 s, results c0..c3 in call order, a read after a write sees it, plus parallel_groups cases); ai_core::batch_runs_its_calls_and_combines_their_results; ai_core::tool_search_loads_from_the_next_call_on_this_branch (first request has tool_search and not the tool, second declares it last, entry.loaded, a sibling branch loads nothing); ai_core::mcp::tests::bm25_ranks_deferred_tools_by_relevance (ranking, plural, camelCase, stop words, search() skips loaded tools, tool_schemas appends loads); session::loaded_tests::loaded_tools_follow_the_active_branch; ai_core::llm::tests::cache_markers_land_on_the_three_breakpoints; config::tests::cache_and_defer_are_opt_in; tui::app::tests::parallel_rows_settle_by_id_in_any_order. rusti --self-test OK (its list_dir row settles before the run_command row). cargo clippy: no new warnings.
decisions: Improved on Pi's 'execute every prepared call concurrently': only adjacent parallel-safe calls overlap and any other call is a barrier in its place, so call order still means what the model meant without Pi's per-file mutation queue.
ToolStart/ToolEnd ids come from a process-wide counter, not the provider's call id: delegate sub-agents emit rows while the parent's are pending, and providers reuse ids like call_0.
The batch tool is expanded in step 1 rather than executed as a tool, so its calls get the same rows, permissions, plan-mode refusals and grouping as direct calls.
tool_search is handled in run_call (it needs the active path's loads) and runs alone; it is not gated and works in plan mode, the tools it loads stay gated.

Anthropic markers also go on a trailing tool result (Pi marks only user/assistant text), so a tool loop's newest results are cached for the next request; compaction sends the same markers since its prefix is the conversation's.
Cache mode is a Client field set from the profile (main, /model), not a global like vision, so parallel tests cannot leak markers into each other's requests.
